To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We have developed an Earth observation approach to study past human occupation in arid lands, and we present preliminary results from the central Sahara.

the use of high-resolution imagery is crucial in the study of archaeological sites in the Central Sahara and that the integration of high- and medium-resolution data is a promising approach for the reconstruction of the landscape.

the study area is a very important area for archaeological and paleo-environmental research, that the study area has a very complex and diverse geomorphological setting, that the use of satellite images can help to identify and classify archaeological and paleo-hydrological features in the study area, and that the use of different satellite images can help us to better understand the geomorphological setting and the paleo-hydrology of the study area.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the application of Earth observation methods for the identification of archaeological features and landscape reconstruction in an area of the Sahara where fieldwork is difficult, and where the archaeological record is poorly documented.
the development of a new approach to study human-environment interactions in the Sahara, based on the use of remote sensing and geomorphological techniques.
the use of remote sensing for the reconstruction of past human-environment interactions in the Central Sahara.

the combination of different satellite data and GIS tools provides a powerful method for the study of the relationship between human occupation, landscape and climate in the Central Sahara, and in other arid regions.
the combination of medium- and very high-resolution satellite imagery is an effective tool for the identification and mapping of archaeological features in the Sahara.
this region is characterized by an abundance of archaeological features and a wide range of geomorphological settings that can be used for landscape reconstruction and human-environment interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of remote sensing techniques can be a useful tool to study past human-landscape interactions in arid lands.

the integration of high- and medium-resolution satellite imagery and geomorphological data provides a valuable tool for the study of the late Holocene landscape and human-environment interactions in arid lands.
satellite imagery, in combination with other sources of information (e.g., field data, historical documents), is an important source for understanding the past and present landscape of the Sahara.
The main takeaway from our work is that

high- and medium-resolution satellite imagery can be a powerful and cost-effective tool for the investigation and mapping of archaeological sites and landscape features, even in remote regions such as the Central Sahara.
high and medium resolution remote sensing data can be used to identify, map and classify archaeological features and to reconstruct paleo-hydrology and vegetation patterns.
satellite imagery can be used to identify and map archaeological features and to provide a preliminary understanding of the geomorphological context of these sites.
